newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Dutch launch A$2 bln takeover for Australia's TNT.
newsitem.headline: Dutch launch A$2 bln takeover for Australia's TNT.

text.p: Dutch telecommunications and postal group Koninklijke PTT Nederland NV (KPN) launched a A$2 billion (US$1.6 billion) takeover bid on Wednesday for worldwide Australian transport giant TNT Ltd.
TNT said in a joint statement with KPN that it would recommend shareholders accept KPN's A$2.45 per share offer, which was at a 50 percent premium to TNT's previous closing share price.

KPN and TNT said the bid represented a multiple of 19.1 times TNT's earnings before interest, tax and abnormal items in the year to June 30, 1996, and a multiple of 2.6 times net assets per share as at June 30.
The agreement followed long, strategic discussions between KPN and TNT about the benefits of combining TNT's businesses with KPN's postal subsidiary, TNT and KPN said in the statement.
"It will create a new global force in the time-sensitive distribution and logistics industry, ranking in the top four worldwide," they said.
The enlarged KPN would offer services in 200 countries with its own operations in 47 countries and would be the largest time-sensitive courier and postal group in Europe.
"This proposal represents an outstanding opportunity to create a strong global transportation group," TNT managing director David Mortimer said.
"For TNT shareholders, it delivers premium value," he said.
The KPN offer for TNT's preference shares includes the A$2.45 cash plus a 6.2 cent per share dividend from TNT for the period ending November 30, 1996.

Shareholders and brokers immediately welcomed the bid, shunting its share price 49 percent higher to A$2.44 in frantic early trade. Brokers said KPN appeared to have paid a strong price and they predicted the bid would be successful.
"I would have thought that's a sensational deal and shareholders won't be able to get out quick enough," said Stephen Streeter, James Capel director of institutional sales.
"It's fairly dramatic. They're certainly not penny pinching," said Kevin Massey, institutional dealer at ABN AMRO Hoare Govett.
PTT Post, a unit of KPN, said in the joint statement it would manage the combined worldwide operations.

"This new group will allow PTT Post to broaden the scope of its activities from mainly domestic postal operations to worldwide time-sensitive distribution and logistics," PTT Post chief executive Ad Scheepbouwer said in the statement.
KPN said it would fund the takeover from working capital and and a 2.25 billion guilders (A$1.7 billion) revolving credit facility arranged and underwritten by Goldman Sachs.
